title: Brief special meeting moves to closed session
subtitle: Closed session on negotiation, legal, litigation and land matters; one councillor recused from a Land Tribunal item.
overview: Council held a short special meeting on June 24, 2024. It opened at 12:09 p.m. and adjourned at 12:14 p.m. The Mayor gave a land acknowledgement, and there was no mayoral business or updates.

The only substantive step was authorizing a closed session right after the meeting. It covered five matters: one involving confidential information to be applied to a negotiation, two legal advice and potential litigation matters, a land acquisition matter, and one more legal advice matter added to the agenda that day. The Municipal Act, 2001 allows councils to meet privately on such topics.

One councillor declared a pecuniary interest in the closed-session item on an Ontario Land Tribunal matter. The reason given was that it might overlap with another item on the agenda and cause a conflict. The councillor took no part in the discussion or vote on that item.
No decisions were made in public. Residents should not expect public outcomes from this meeting unless council reports on them later.

decisions.detail: Council authorized a closed session after the special meeting to consider five negotiation, legal, litigation and land acquisition matters under Sections 239 (c), (e), (f) and (k) of the Municipal Act, 2001.

debate: There was no debate on the substance of any item. The meeting dealt only with procedure.
A councillor declared a conflict on the Ontario Land Tribunal legal advice item, saying the advice might relate to a later matter where a conflict could arise.
When asked, the councillor said the concern was not about owned properties. The councillor chose to stay out of the discussion as a precaution because it was unclear whether a conflict existed.
